question.problem: On average, every batch of televisions has $5$ defective televisions in a television factory. What is the probability that the factory will produce more than $2$ defective televisions in the next batch? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that defective televisions occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of televisions produced with defects. Since the average rate is $5$ televisions with defects per batch, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of televisions with defects can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =5,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(5).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{5}^{x}{e}^{-5}}{x!}
$$

To compute $P(X>2),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>2)=1-P(X\le 2)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =P(X\in {0,1,2}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2) \\  & =\frac{{5}^{0}{e}^{-5}}{0!}+\frac{{5}^{1}{e}^{-5}}{1!}+\frac{{5}^{2}{e}^{-5}}{2!} \\  & ≈0.125\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of finding more than $2$ defective televisions in the next batch is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>2) & =1-P(X\le 2) \\  & ≈1-0.125 \\  & =0.875\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
